profile.research_note: Session 2026-09-03: this is the cooperative's headquarters/central office; treated as the facility itself given no separate data-center-specific address is published for a co-op of this size.

reading.body:
Marquette-Adams Telephone Cooperative operates a data-center facility in Wisconsin with zero reported megawatts of capacity, indicating either unreported power draw or a facility too small for public disclosure thresholds.

The cooperative runs its facility from its headquarters in Oxford as a combined central office and data operation, a structure typical of rural telephone utilities that have repurposed legacy telecom infrastructure. Rural cooperatives often lack the capital and grid access to build dedicated, large-scale data centers, so they repurpose existing buildings and connections to serve local enterprise or cloud edge computing needs.

The zero-megawatt rating reflects a gap in how small facilities are tracked. Rural data infrastructure that serves real computing workloads may consume meaningful power but falls below the reporting requirements that apply to larger operators. This obscures the distributed nature of the actual data infrastructure footprint in the United States.

The data does not reveal what workloads this facility serves, what its actual power consumption is, or whether it connects to broader AI compute chains. It confirms only that a rural cooperative has categorized itself as a data-center operator, which is relevant to understanding where compute lives outside major metropolitan clusters.
